header: This file decides how an answer written by the language model is PRESENTED. Pure functions, no database, no React, safe to import from both the server (omnibar.ts) and the browser (AnswerResult.tsx). The model may suggest a presentation (a "display" hint next to its SQL): {"view": "cards" | "table" | "bar", "title": "...", "columns": [{"key": "...", "label": "..."}], "bar": {"label": "<text column>", "value": "<numeric column>"}} The model PROPOSES, I VERIFY against the real result here and fall back to a layout chosen from the shape of the data. So a missing, malformed or wrong hint can never break an answer, and: GUARANTEE: every column the SQL returned is shown, exactly once. A hint can reorder and retitle the columns; it can never hide one.

symbols.name: departmentGroups
symbols.sig: export function departmentGroups<T extends { department?: string | null; departmentCode?: string | null }>(people: T[]): DepartmentGroup<T>[] | null
symbols.generics: T extends { department?: string | null; departmentCode?: string | null }
doc: When a list of people falls into a few CONSECUTIVE department blocks (executives first under one code, then the sections), I return those blocks so the page can show one heading per block instead of repeating the department on every card. I never change the order. Returns null when grouping would not help: fewer than 4 people, someone with no department, more than 6 blocks, or blocks averaging fewer than 2 people.

symbols.name: filterRows
symbols.sig: export function filterRows(rows: Row[], columns: DisplayColumn[], query: string): Row[]
doc: I let the filter box above a list take several things at once, separated by a comma (or ; | or the word "or"): "gm, dgm, agm". Each one is either

- a DESIGNATION (in any case, with or without dots: gm, dgm, agm, ed, dic, Dy. general manager, asst.general manager, sr mgr ...): the rows with exactly that designation, however it is spelled in the list; or
- text, found anywhere in the row as before (a name, a ticket, a department, a code); dots and spaces do not matter ("asst.general" finds "Asst. General").
A designation and a word can be combined ("roy gm"). See designationFilter.ts for the rules.

symbols.name: isSingleRowTable
symbols.sig: export function isSingleRowTable(kind: string | undefined, count: number | undefined, hasTable: boolean): boolean
doc: The big number and "N rows." at the top of a table answer say how many rows there are. For ONE row (a lookup of one person or one ticket) that is noise, since the table already shows it, so I hide it in that case only: a count answer ("how many ...", a single number) and any list of 2 or more keep theirs.
